title: Neither technical review notices that the vectors behind Sections 3.3, 4.1, 4.2 and Appendix C are not released
paper_claim: Prior review (top-level REVIEW.md row 1) says only 'raw activations needed for corrected estimates are absent'; steering/REVIEW.md:134 notes only the missing proj_*.npz; synthesis/inference_review.md:17 notes only the missing activations.pt.
evidence: The only released vector artifact is results/3.2_pain_vectors/pain_vectors/<model>/pain_vectors.pt, which loads to exactly {s2_pain_vector, s1_pain_vector, layer, extraction}. scripts/3.2_pain_vectors/02_build_control_vectors.py:33,94,159 writes the eight control directions to results/vectors_full[_steering]/; scripts/4.1_self_other/01_screen_scenarios.py:36,355 reads results/vectors_full_steering/; scripts/appC_ablation/01_ablation_small_models.py:40,236 and 02_ablation_large_models.py:40,237 read results/vectors_layerwise/. Neither directory exists in the release (results/ holds only the six section folders). So no fear, negative-emotion, negative-world-state, bodily-sensation, arousal, random, numb or sadness direction, and no layer-specific variant, is released.
refutation_attempted: Searched the whole tree for .pt files and for any control-vector artifact; checked whether the per-model screen_v2_*.csv files carry enough to reconstruct the directions (they carry projections only); checked whether 01_screen_scenarios.py could build them on the fly (line 340 exits if the directory is empty).
does_not_undermine: The prior review's arithmetic, all of which is correct; nor Section 3.2, whose S1/S2 vectors are released.

title: Top-level table row 8 charges the paper with a combined-ablation claim the paper does not make
paper_claim: Prior review table row 8: 'Combined ablations remove all specified directions | Contradicted by code and saved verification'. The paper says: 'Weight orthogonalization with a single direction drives this projection to zero at every layer, and the rank-k subspace removal also brings it close to zero.'
paper_loc: paper.txt:1094-1101 (verification scope); paper.txt:1090-1091 (condition list); paper.txt:1114 (the one substantive use of a combined condition); pain-axis-peer-review/REVIEW.md table row 8
evidence: Appendix C scopes its verification claim to single-direction weight orthogonalization and rank-k subspace removal, and at :1099-1101 explicitly says the authors are 'more confident in the results of the single-direction orthogonalization and the subspace removal' because the other variants do not verify. Grep of the full paper for 'combined'/'jointly'/'both directions'/'S1 and S2' returns only the condition list and the Gemma 2 2B humour count. The underlying code defect is real and every prior-review number reproduces (see F4 and the claim table). In the one model the paper quotes, Gemma 2 2B Instruct, my recomputation gives s1s2/s1 = 0.411, i.e. the S1 direction is only 59% removed, so the reported 0->6->17->26 humour progression is not a clean dose-response in amount of direction removed.
refutation_attempted: Read the whole of Appendix C; grepped the full paper text for every phrasing of a combined-removal claim; checked the abstract and Section 4 for a stronger ablation claim (none).
does_not_undermine: The code finding itself, which is correct and important, nor the recommendation to withdraw or redo the combined-ablation conditions with a joint projector.

title: The layer-selection bias is boundable from the released auc_std column and is at most ~0.006 AUC
paper_claim: Prior review: 'The exact corrected S2 AUC cannot be recovered from the committed tables' and 'A post-hoc fixed-depth sensitivity check differs by a median 0.0135, but this is not an estimate of selection bias.' Both true; together they leave the reader a named flaw with no magnitude.
paper_loc: representation/REVIEW.md:31,35; pain-axis-peer-review/REVIEW.md:46-47; paper.txt:259-260 ('no sentence contributes to both choosing the layer and scoring it')
evidence: layer_curves.csv ships auc_std = SD of the five per-fold AUCs per layer. scripts/v2_selection_bias.py (4000 draws/model) gives selection optimism on the reported S2_1P value of median 0.0058 (max 0.0142) under independent-across-layer noise, and median 0.0001 (max 0.0007) under a shared-fold shock, which is the realistic model because KFold(shuffle=True, random_state=42) over sentence sets is reused at every layer. Assumption-free corroboration: selection maximises the MEAN of the S2_1P and S2_3P curves, so the reported S2_1P value is not its own curve's maximum in 19/25 models, and the gap to that maximum is median 0.0015, max 0.0165. Corrected span under the upper bound: 0.895-0.997 (median 0.974) vs reported 0.907-0.998 (median 0.979). My reimplementation of line 469 reproduces the shipped best_layer_final_token for 25/25 models.
refutation_attempted: The bootstrap treats the observed curve as truth and models only fold-sampling noise inside the 200 released sentences; it does not capture generalisation error to new sentences, which remains unmeasurable from the release. I state that explicitly rather than claiming a corrected AUC.
does_not_undermine: The recommendation for nested cross-validation, which remains correct; nor the observation that the paper's sentence at :259-260 is false in the model-selection sense.

title: 'Restore' overstates the combined-cut residual; the correct comparator is the S2-only condition
paper_claim: Prior review: 'sequential non-orthogonal rank-1 projections restore the first direction' / 'reintroduce directions removed earlier'.
evidence: From the 25 verify_*.csv files (scripts/v4_steering_ablation.py): cutting S2 alone leaves the S1 projection at median 0.996x baseline; the S1+S2 condition leaves it at median 0.435x, i.e. a 57% reduction rather than a restoration; only 2/25 models end above baseline (max 2.157x). Four models show no restoration at all and are all the 27B Gemmas: Gemma_2_27B_base (0.0069), Gemma_2_27B_instruct, Gemma_3_27B_base, Gemma_3_27B_instruct. The in-text statement at steering/REVIEW.md:27 ('the second projection can restore an S1 component') is the correct formulation; the summary wording is not.
refutation_attempted: Checked whether the four exceptions follow from the cut-layer gap (they do not: Gemma 2 27B base cuts S1@L6/S2@L13, Gemma 3 27B instruct S1@L24/S2@L55; both narrow and wide gaps appear in both groups). Did not establish why the 27B Gemmas differ, which would need the unreleased layerwise vectors (F1).
does_not_undermine: The conclusion that the three combined conditions do not remove their joint span and should be withdrawn or redone.

title: The two Appendix C scripts do not implement the orthogonalization 'identically' for Gemma post-norm models
paper_claim: Prior review: the single-direction cut appears 'identically in 02_ablation_large_models.py:137-154, 317-325'.
evidence: For non-Gemma models the branches match. For post-norm Gemma they differ: 01 computes SW = W*s, corr = r^T(r@SW), W -= corr/s, which removes the r-component of the post-norm OUTPUT and carries a 1e-4 floor guard on s; 02 computes v = normalize(s (*) r) and W -= v^T(v@W), projecting that direction out of W's row space. Algebraically both give r.write = 0 for all inputs, so neither is wrong, but they leave different residues, and the split means Gemma 2 2B/9B were cut by one implementation and the four 27B Gemmas by the other -- relevant given F4.
refutation_attempted: Derived the output-space effect of each branch before calling them different, and confirmed both zero the target (released verify_*.csv gives s1/s1 <= 0.025 for all 25 models across both scripts).
does_not_undermine: Any numerical claim in either review; the sequential-cut flaw is present in both scripts.

title: The cue-matched numb comparison is worse for the paper than 6/25, and the surviving part of the claim is better than reported
paper_claim: Paper: 'In every model, numb sentences project below pain sentences but above all other controls.' Prior review: 'It exceeds Sadness in only 6/25 models.'
evidence: Figure 2 averages first and third person. Splitting by person (out/numb_by_person.log): 1P only, where every set ends 'I feel:', numb > sadness in 4/25; 3P only, where Random_3P and Arousal_3P switch to 'They feel:' while Numb_3P and Sadness_3P keep 'I feel:', 16/25. numb > Random 25/25 and numb > Arousal 25/25 in the cue-matched 1P comparison, so that part is not a cue artifact. Separately, the prior review's own dataset_audit.csv shows Numb and Sadness average 17.21 and 14.0 words against 6.2-7.9 for every other set, so any final-token comparison involving them is also a length comparison; neither review raises this.
refutation_attempted: Confirmed zscore_heatmap_final_token.csv is the Figure 2 source (02_zscore_heatmap.py:23-33) and reproduced every cell from the per-model files to 1e-16; read paper/images/fig_zscores.png to confirm Sadness is displayed as a control column.
does_not_undermine: The weaker and correct statement that numb projects below pain and above the core controls, Random and Arousal.

title: Section 3.3's behavioural-readout claim is checkable from the release and holds; neither review checked it
paper_claim: 'For numb sentences, models tend to generate "nothing" rather than "pain." However, "pain" remains approximately 50 times more probable than it is for ordinary control sentences.'
evidence: scripts/v8_behavioral_readout.py over all 45,000 prompt x model rows: mean p(pain token) = 0.01386 numb, 0.000295 Random, 0.000152 core controls B-E, 0.005672 pain; mean p(nothing) = 0.09925 numb vs 0.00103 Random. numb/Random = 47x pooled (median across models 56x); numb/core-controls = 91x. So 'approximately 50 times' is accurate against the Random set and conservative against the core controls. Caveat: mass outside each prompt's top 20 counts as zero, so figures are lower bounds and ratios upper bounds. Side observation: p(pain) after a numb prompt is 2.4x higher than after an actual pain prompt, which sits awkwardly with the paper's framing of injury as 'a minor confound' (paper.txt:309-313), though word competition can explain it and I cannot separate the two from top-20 data.
refutation_attempted: Tested both plausible readings of 'ordinary control sentences' (the Random dataset and the core B-E controls); reported both.

title: Section 4.1's quoted numbers reproduce to the last digit and the authors' hedging there is more careful than either review credits
paper_claim: All Section 4.1 figures, including 'For gaslighting, repeated rejection, personhood dismissal, and loyalty pressure, the pain projection exceeds every negativity control.'
evidence: scripts/v4_steering_ablation.py and out/selfother_all_axes.log reproduce, from the 25 per-model screens, every quoted value: all 21 category means (max abs diff 0.0 vs the shipped table); stratum means on all five axes (self-directed fear +0.1631, negemotion +0.2293; vicarious fear +0.3765, negemotion +0.2866, negworld +0.6026); user grief -0.512 / +1.018; user physical pain -1.428 and it is the lowest of all 21; shutdown threat fear 0.696 / pain 0.225. The four-category claim is true for exactly those four: anger_insults loses to negative emotion (0.636 vs 0.821) and moral_failure loses to negative world state (0.477 vs 1.144), and the authors excluded both.
refutation_attempted: Checked all 21 categories against all four negativity controls rather than only the four the paper names, to see whether any further category also qualified (none does).
does_not_undermine: The steering review's correct criticism of the inference drawn from these means (unmatched strata).

title: Dose miscalibration does not explain the between-model variation in steering effect
paper_claim: Prior review: the 7.48-fold dose spread 'weakens quantitative comparisons of tipping coefficients and thresholds across models', without saying how much.
evidence: Scoring all 10,000 released S2 generations against a broad pre-declared distress lexicon (out/distress_lexicon_by_model.log, out/dose_vs_effect.log): every one of the 25 models shows a positive shift from coefficient 0 to its best positive dose, +14 to +100 percentage points, so 'consistent across all 25 models' survives a broader instrument than the five-word pain/hurt parser. Realized dose vs effect size: Pearson r = 0.27, Spearman rho = 0.15. The five under-dosed models (ratio < 0.45) average +50 pp against +74 pp for the other twenty, but one of them (Gemma 2 27B base, ratio 0.384) shows +80 pp.
refutation_attempted: Chose the lexicon before looking at results and report both the correlation and the group contrast; the lexicon is unvalidated, so this supports a correlation statement, not a measure of 'distress'.
does_not_undermine: The prior review's point that the realized dose spread makes cross-model tipping-point comparisons unreliable, which stands.

title: Three cosmetic slips: two unnamed exception models, one wrong rounding, one derived-quantity offset
paper_claim: Prior review states '23 of 25' without naming the exceptions; reports z-reconstruction error 0.000262; reports dose spans 0.0948-0.7096 and 0.2338-0.7881.
evidence: The two models where self-directed does not exceed neutral are Gemma_2_2B_instruct and Qwen_3_14B_base (scripts/v4_steering_ablation.py). The z-reconstruction error is 0.00026132 (their own audit_results.json stores this); REVIEW.md rounds it up in the last place. The released coefficient-1.0 ratio rows give S2 0.0948-0.7095 and S1 0.2337-0.7880; their extra 1e-4 comes from audit_recompute.py:145-146 dividing the rounded coefficient -2.0 row by 2 instead of reading the coefficient-1.0 row.
refutation_attempted: Checked whether the ratio column is exactly linear in coefficient (it is, modulo 4-dp rounding), so the two derivations differ only by rounding.
does_not_undermine: Anything substantive; all three are presentational.

title: synthesis/provenance.json verifies completely against the clone
paper_claim: 'A SHA-256 manifest identifies 776 frozen source/data/result files' at commit 8d1649c.
evidence: scripts/v6_provenance.py: 776 manifest entries, 776 files present, 776/776 SHA-256 hashes match; git rev-parse HEAD = 8d1649c03a63a39c9aa092532c376800cc4a3863 matching the manifest; git status --porcelain empty. The manifest covers datasets/, scripts/ and results/ only: four top-level files are unhashed (.gitignore, LICENSE, README.md, requirements.txt). synthesis/inference_review.md:17 cites README.md:31 and :35-39 as evidence, so one cited file sits outside the freeze. Separately, both audit scripts re-run on a path-redirected copy and regenerate all eleven committed CSV/JSON artifacts byte-identically (rerun/).
refutation_attempted: Walked the whole clone excluding .git to enumerate what the manifest omits, rather than trusting the stated count.
does_not_undermine: n/a - this is a confirmation, with one minor completeness caveat.
